result.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization
result.summary: Link prediction remains difficult in sparse graphs, where diffusion heuristics lack connectivity and geometric methods suffer spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators. We introduce Concorde, an energy-based framework that resolves this by decomposing link likelihood into three structurally decoupled branches: (i) a parameter-free spectral anchor that establishes permutation-invariant topological stability; (ii) a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable $\mathbb{H}^{d_h}_{c_h} \times \mathbb{S}^{d_s}_{c_s}$ product manifold, regularized by a feature-aware Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy; and (iii) a continuous vector field on the tangent bundle of hyperbolic space for non-local structural alignment across topological gaps. The branches are fused via learned gating and trained with an N-pair ranking loss aligned with retrieval-style evaluation. Across five benchmarks spanning sparse, dense, featureless, and attributed regimes, Concorde establishes state-of-the-art early retrieval precision, nearly doubling P@10% over leading baselines in sparse settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Concorde，一个能量式链接预测框架：把链接似然拆成无参数谱锚点、混合曲率乘积流形上的残差（以特征感知 Ollivier-Ricci 曲率代理正则）和双曲切丛上的连续向量场三分支，用学习门控融合并以 N-pair 排序损失训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其混合曲率乘积流形表示与能量最小化的解耦分支融合，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态的表示几何及多路推理状态整合存在远域启发，但需核查其几何先验能否脱离图链接任务迁移。
